# Specifies the base image for the build environment. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, well-supported choice.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during the build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, compilers (GCC/G++), version control (Git),
# networking tools (wget), security certificates, and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# Cleaning up apt lists reduces the final image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    git \
    make \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create and set a temporary working directory for compiling the application and its dependencies.
WORKDIR /tmp/build

# Download, build, and install METIS 4.0.3 from source.
# This version requires specific compiler flags and manual installation of the library and header
# to a system-wide location (/usr/local) so that other builds (like MFEM) can find it.
RUN wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make CFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC' OPTFLAGS='-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp metis.h /usr/local/include/

# Download, build, and install Hypre 2.28.0 from source.
# It is configured with specific flags to disable Fortran and enable 64-bit integer support.
# The configure script automatically detects the system's MPI installation.
RUN wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install

# Clone and build the MFEM (Modular Finite Element Methods) library version 4.7 from source.
# The 'parallel' make target builds the library with MPI support enabled. The build system
# will automatically find the previously installed METIS and Hypre dependencies in /usr/local.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc)

# Clone and build the Laghos application.
# The build is linked against the MFEM library compiled in the previous step.
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    MFEM_DIR=/tmp/build/mfem make -j$(nproc)

# Prepare the final application environment. This includes creating a dedicated app directory,
# copying the Laghos executable to a location on the system's PATH, and moving the necessary
# input data files. The temporary build directory is then removed to keep the final image clean.
RUN mkdir -p /app && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/data/* /app/ && \
    rm -rf /tmp/build

# Set environment variables required for OpenMPI to run correctly as the root user inside a container.
# These settings are standard for containerized HPC environments.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set the final working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

# Specifies the base image for the build environment. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, well-supported choice.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during the build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, compilers (GCC/G++), version control (Git),
# networking tools (wget), security certificates, and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# Cleaning up apt lists reduces the final image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    git \
    make \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create and set a temporary working directory for compiling the application and its dependencies.
WORKDIR /tmp/build

# Download, build, and install METIS 4.0.3 from source.
# FIX: CFLAGS are updated to include the current directory (-I.) for header discovery and to
# suppress implicit function declaration errors. The path for copying metis.h is also corrected.
RUN wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make CFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -I. -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/

# Download, build, and install Hypre 2.28.0 from source.
# It is configured with specific flags to disable Fortran and enable 64-bit integer support.
# The configure script automatically detects the system's MPI installation.
RUN wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install

# Clone and build the MFEM (Modular Finite Element Methods) library version 4.7 from source.
# The 'parallel' make target builds the library with MPI support enabled. The build system
# will automatically find the previously installed METIS and Hypre dependencies in /usr/local.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc)

# Clone and build the Laghos application.
# The build is linked against the MFEM library compiled in the previous step.
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    MFEM_DIR=/tmp/build/mfem make -j$(nproc)

# Prepare the final application environment. This includes creating a dedicated app directory,
# copying the Laghos executable to a location on the system's PATH, and moving the necessary
# input data files. The temporary build directory is then removed to keep the final image clean.
RUN mkdir -p /app && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/data/* /app/ && \
    rm -rf /tmp/build

# Set environment variables required for OpenMPI to run correctly as the root user inside a container.
# These settings are standard for containerized HPC environments.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set the final working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

# Specifies the base image for the build environment. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, well-supported choice.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during the build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, compilers (GCC/G++), version control (Git),
# networking tools (wget), security certificates, and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# Cleaning up apt lists reduces the final image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    git \
    make \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create and set a temporary working directory for compiling the application and its dependencies.
WORKDIR /tmp/build

# Download, build, and install METIS 4.0.3 from source.
# FIX: Use OPTFLAGS instead of CFLAGS. This allows the METIS Makefile to correctly construct
# the full compiler flags, including the necessary include paths, preventing header not found errors.
RUN wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/

# Download, build, and install Hypre 2.28.0 from source.
# It is configured with specific flags to disable Fortran and enable 64-bit integer support.
# The configure script automatically detects the system's MPI installation.
RUN wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install

# Clone and build the MFEM (Modular Finite Element Methods) library version 4.7 from source.
# The 'parallel' make target builds the library with MPI support enabled. The build system
# will automatically find the previously installed METIS and Hypre dependencies in /usr/local.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc)

# Clone and build the Laghos application.
# The build is linked against the MFEM library compiled in the previous step.
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    MFEM_DIR=/tmp/build/mfem make -j$(nproc)

# Prepare the final application environment. This includes creating a dedicated app directory,
# copying the Laghos executable to a location on the system's PATH, and moving the necessary
# input data files. The temporary build directory is then removed to keep the final image clean.
RUN mkdir -p /app && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/data/* /app/ && \
    rm -rf /tmp/build

# Set environment variables required for OpenMPI to run correctly as the root user inside a container.
# These settings are standard for containerized HPC environments.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set the final working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \

    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/data/* /app/ && \

# Specifies the base image for the build environment. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, well-supported choice.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during the build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, compilers (GCC/G++), version control (Git),
# networking tools (wget), security certificates, and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# Cleaning up apt lists reduces the final image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    git \
    make \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create and set a temporary working directory for compiling the application and its dependencies.
WORKDIR /tmp/build

# Download, build, and install METIS 4.0.3 from source.
# Use OPTFLAGS instead of CFLAGS. This allows the METIS Makefile to correctly construct
# the full compiler flags, including the necessary include paths, preventing header not found errors.
RUN wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/

# Download, build, and install Hypre 2.28.0 from source.
# It is configured with specific flags to disable Fortran and enable 64-bit integer support.
# FIX: Manually copy the generated HYPRE_config.h, as 'make install' may not reliably
# place it in the system include path, causing downstream build failures.
RUN wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cp HYPRE_config.h /usr/local/include/

# Clone and build the MFEM (Modular Finite Element Methods) library version 4.7 from source.
# Explicitly provide paths to the system-installed Hypre and METIS dependencies,
# as the MFEM Makefile does not automatically detect them in /usr/local.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local

# Clone and build the Laghos application.
# The build is linked against the MFEM library compiled in the previous step.
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    MFEM_DIR=/tmp/build/mfem make -j$(nproc)

# Prepare the final application environment. This includes creating a dedicated app directory,
# copying the Laghos executable to a location on the system's PATH, and moving the necessary
# input data files. The temporary build directory is then removed to keep the final image clean.
RUN mkdir -p /app && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/data/* /app/ && \
    rm -rf /tmp/build

# Set environment variables required for OpenMPI to run correctly as the root user inside a container.
# These settings are standard for containerized HPC environments.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set the final working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

flux-minicluster-manifest
# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the Laghos HPC proxy application
# within a single pod on a Kubernetes cluster, managed by the Flux Operator.
# It is configured for a generic AWS CPU instance environment.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance
  name: laghos-cpu-experiment
  # Deploy to the default namespace as requested
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster job. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks (processes) to run across the cluster.
  # Flux will schedule these tasks across the available slots in the pods.
  tasks: 4

  # Ensure strict logging for better debugging during the experiment.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Set to false to keep the pods and services running after the job completes
  # for post-run inspection and data retrieval.
  cleanup: false

  # Define the single container that will run the HPC application.
  # The Flux Operator will inject a "flux-view" sidecar for the broker.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      # The command to be executed by Flux. The Flux Operator will prepend `flux run -n <tasks>`.
      # This runs the laghos application with the specified mesh file.
      # Additional arguments can be added here as needed for the experiment.
      command: laghos -m cube_311_hex.mesh

      # The working directory is set to the location of the Laghos executable
      # and its data files within the container image.
      workingDir: /laghos

      # The launcher flag MUST be false. A launcher pod is intended for
      # submitting to an external cluster and is not used in this scenario.
      launcher: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest is optimized to run the Laghos HPC
# application on a single, powerful AWS Graviton (ARM) instance.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance
  name: laghos-cpu-experiment
  # Deploy to the default namespace as requested
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster job. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks, scaled to 64 to fully utilize the vCPUs
  # of the selected hpc7g.16xlarge instance for performance optimization.
  tasks: 64

  # Ensure strict logging for better debugging.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Keep the pods running after the job completes for inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Flux-specific configurations
  flux:
    container:
      # Specify the ARM64-compatible flux-view image, which is required
      # for running on AWS Graviton instances (like hpc7g.16xlarge).
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Pod-level specifications
  pod:
    # Schedule the job on a specific high-performance, CPU-optimized
    # AWS instance type to meet the optimization goal.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # Define the single container that will run the HPC application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos

      # Corrected command to run laghos with performance analysis (-pa)
      # on the specified mesh file.
      command: laghos -pa -m cube_311_hex.mesh

      # FIX: Correct the working directory to /app, where the laghos executable
      # and its mesh data files are located inside the container.
      workingDir: /app

      # The launcher flag MUST be false for this execution model.
      launcher: false

# This manifest is corrected to resolve an 'Exec format error' and an
# invalid application argument from the previous attempt.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: laghos-cpu-experiment
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The MiniCluster will run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # FIX: Adjusted the number of tasks to 48 to match the vCPU count of the
  # new x86_64 instance type (c7a.12xlarge).
  tasks: 48

  # Keep the pods running after the job completes for inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Ensure strict logging for better debugging.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod-level specifications
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      # FIX: Switched to an AMD (x86_64) instance type to resolve the CPU
      # architecture mismatch that caused the 'Exec format error'.
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

  # Define the single container that will run the HPC application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      # FIX: Removed the invalid '-o 4' argument from the command as it is
      # not a recognized option by the laghos application.
      command: laghos -pa -m cube_311_hex.mesh
      workingDir: /app
      launcher: false

# REMOVED: The flux.container spec for an ARM-specific image has been removed.
# The Flux Operator will now use its default x86_64 compatible image, which is
# appropriate for the selected c7a.12xlarge node.

Decision 2: RETRY

Agent's Rationale: The previous ARM-based run (118.2 on hpc7g.16xlarge) significantly outperformed the AMD run (98.4 on c7a.12xlarge). This suggests the application is better optimized for the Graviton3 architecture. This attempt will test another 64-core Graviton3 instance (m7g.16xlarge) which has double the memory. This will help determine if the application is memory-bandwidth limited, which could lead to a performance improvement over the previous best score.
